title: Director of People Operations
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.



We’re bringing on a Director of People Operations to be the operational engine of our People function, driving the full spectrum of people programs. Total rewards is your core strength and the capability that complements our existing People team, but this role goes well beyond comp and benefits. You’ll build and scale the processes, infrastructure, and programs that support a fast-moving, global business, and you’ll do it with direct access to business leaders. This is a lean, high-trust role: you’ll report to our VP of People, lead a small team, and operate with the autonomy that comes from being close to the decisions that matter. If you’re energized by building the machine, not just running it, this is your kind of role.



What You'll Do

Total Rewards - Your Core Strength

•     Evolve and steward ALSO's compensation philosophy — job architecture, salary bands, leveling frameworks, and equity programs that work across our US and global teams

•     Lead compensation cycles on a regular cadence: merit, bonus, and additional equity grants, in close partnership with Finance and the VP of People

•     Own benefits strategy end-to-end — plan design, broker and vendor relationships, open enrollment, and ongoing benchmarking to ensure we remain competitive as we grow into new markets

•     Partner with the People Partner and Talent Acquisition on compensation for new hires and promotions, maintaining consistency and fairness at every level



People Operations & People Infrastructure

•     Partner with our People Ops Manager to evolve our HRIS and broader People tech stack, building on the deep investment of these systems and experience on the team — data integrity, system integrations, and self-service tooling that makes life easier for employees and managers alike

•     Build and maintain scalable People Ops processes across the full employee lifecycle: onboarding, offboarding, leave administration, performance cycles, and internal mobility

•     Ensure compliance across federal, state, local, and international employment law requirements — with a particular focus on our growing global footprint

•     Keep our people infrastructure lean and smart; we're not building for headcount, we're building for impact



Employee Experience & Engagement

•     Partner with the People Partner to develop and run employee engagement programs, recognition initiatives, and feedback loops that reflect ALSO's culture and values

•     Use people data and surveys to surface insights that help leadership make better decisions about our team



Team Leadership & Strategic People Partnership

•     Serve as a trusted advisor to the VP of People and senior leadership on compensation, org design, and people operations

•     Translate complexity into clarity — whether that's communicating a new comp framework to the team or presenting a benefits recommendation to the exec team

•     Lead and develop a small, high-impact team: setting clear priorities, modeling operational excellence, and creating an environment where people do their best work

•     Be a player-coach: you set direction and you also do the work, and you're proud of both



What You’ll Bring

We're looking for someone with deep roots in total rewards and the breadth to hold everything else that comes with running People Ops at a global, pre-IPO company. You'll likely bring:



•     8–12 years of progressive People or People Ops experience, with at least 5–7 years focused specifically on compensation, benefits, or total rewards

•     Experience leading people and programs in a high-growth or startup environment — you know what it means to build, not just maintain

•     Deep knowledge of compensation design, equity programs (ISOs, RSUs), and benefits administration in a multi-state and/or international context

•     Comfort operating across multiple geographies and navigating the compliance complexity that comes with global teams

•     Strong analytical skills — you can build a comp model and you know how to use data to tell a story that lands with leadership

•     High emotional intelligence and discretion; people trust you with sensitive information at every level of the org

•     A builder's mindset: you're energized by creating structure where there isn't any, and you don't need a large team to do great work



Nice to Have

•     Experience in EV, or consumer product companies

•     Familiarity with pre-IPO equity compensation and the complexity that comes with it

•     Experience supporting global market entry and the people infrastructure it requires

•     CCP, SHRM-SCP, or CEBS certification


The salary for this position ranges from $180,000 - $230,000 per year, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.

 

This is an onsite position requiring attendance in the office 5 days per week. Once fully ramped and in alignment with their manager, employees may have the opportunity for limited flexibility, including the potential to work remotely up to two days per week, based on business and team needs.

 

Perks & Benefits

 - Robust health coverage — excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by ALSO with FSA & HSA options

 - One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates

 - Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny

 - Flexible time off

 - 401(k) match

Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

focus areas.

• Partner with BTS, Compliance, Privacy, Security, and Procurement to ensure

• Bachelor’s degree in business, healthcare administration, information systems, or

• 7+ years of experience in pharmaceutical patient services, HCP-facing digital

managers/leads or a multi-disciplinary team.
• Demonstrated experience managing vendor relationships and/or digital platform
governance in a regulated (pharma/healthcare) environment.
• Working knowledge of HCP-facing technology ecosystems — portals, EHR/eRx
connectivity, and benefits verification/enrollment workflows.
• Strong stakeholder management skills; ability to influence across IT, brand,
compliance, and operations teams without direct authority, while also leading a
direct team.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with ability to translate technical
concepts for business audiences and vice versa.
Preferred Qualifications
• Familiarity with Salesforce Health Cloud or Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud.
• Experience with EHR/eRx integration models for specialty pharmaceutical
enrollment.
• Experience managing multi-vendor technology ecosystems supporting benefits
verification, prior authorization, or patient access programs.
• Prior experience leading leads/managers (vs. only individual contributors).
• PMP, Agile/Scrum, or vendor/contract management certification a plus.

Purpose:
The Change Management Specialist supports and, for assigned initiatives, leads the execution of change-management strategies that enable adoption, behavior change, and achievement of business outcomes. Working within the AbbVie-wide RISE framework, this role conducts stakeholder and change-impact assessments, supports readiness and engagement planning, develops communications and learning solutions, coordinates change champions and stakeholder activities, and monitors adoption and reinforcement. The Specialist partners with the Director, Associate Director, Manager, project teams, process owners, sponsors, and subject-matter experts from project inception through implementation and stabilization. The Specialist formally reports to the Director, Change Management and receives day-to-day work direction, coaching, or initiative-level supervision from the Associate Director and/or Manager.

Collect, analyze, and report readiness, participation, proficiency, adoption, feedback, behavior-change, and other relevant success metrics, identifying actions to improve adoption and reinforce new behaviors.
Maintain integrated change-management deliverables, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, and action items in alignment with project plans and governance requirements.
Capture lessons learned, contribute reusable assets and case studies, and recommend improvements to change-management tools, templates, and ways of working.
Bachelor’s degree preferred in communications, education, instructional design, organizational development, business, human resources, or related field.
Familiarity with learning, collaboration, content-management, survey, reporting, and project-management tools preferred
3+ years’ experience in change management, organizational development, project management, communications, learning and development, business process improvement, or related discipline.
Experience supporting changes to processes, systems, roles, operating models, or ways of working.
Working knowledge of a structured change-management methodology and willingness to learn and apply the AbbVie-wide RISE framework.
Experience conducting stakeholder interviews, impact assessments, readiness assessments, focus groups, or similar discovery activities.
Demonstrated ability to develop audience-centered communications, presentations, job aids, training materials, and other change deliverables.
Ability to use qualitative and quantitative data to identify adoption barriers and recommend actions.
Strong facilitation, organization, prioritization, collaboration, and follow-through skills.
Ability to work effectively with stakeholders at different organizational levels and across cultures.

Director, IPMO; Associate Director, Change Management; Manager, Change Management; project and program leaders; process owners; subject-matter experts; end users; HR; Communications; Training/Learning; IPMO/PMO; functional stakeholders; change champions/advocates; vendors and contractors.

The Global Business Process Lead, Supply Chain Transformation plays a key role in advancing AbbVie’s supply chain capabilities through process optimization, digital enablement, and transformation initiatives. This individual partners across business and technology teams to help define, shape, and deliver scalable solutions that improve operational performance, visibility, and decision quality across the global supply chain network.
This role requires a strong understanding of end-to-end supply chain processes, the ability to translate business needs into technology requirements, and the ability to translate technical concepts into clear business implications. The ideal candidate will participate in transformation projects, support the design and adoption of data products and AI-enabled capabilities, and help ensure solutions are practical, sustainable, and aligned to business objectives.
Responsibilities
Support and drive strategic supply chain transformation initiatives spanning process redesign, system enhancements, digital enablement, data products, AI-related initiatives, and business integration.
Serve as the business process lead and translator between business and technology teams, helping translate operational needs into clear requirements, priorities, solution designs, and measurable outcomes.
Partner cross-functionally with stakeholders in Finance, Purchasing, Internal and Contract Manufacturing, and Master Data to identify challenges, dependencies, and opportunities for end-to-end improvement.
Design future-state processes and harmonized workflows that improve operational performance, visibility, compliance, service levels, and decision quality across the global supply chain.
Redesign roles and workflows around AI-supported decisions and AI agents, ensuring appropriate governance, accountability, controls, and human oversight.
Analyze performance gaps and use data-driven insights to recommend practical, scalable, and sustainable process and technology solutions.
Support business readiness and adoption through stakeholder engagement, change management, communications, training, and user-experience improvements.
Establish and promote best practices, process standards, and continuous-improvement approaches across global, functional, and local teams.
Build strong partnerships with internal teams and external stakeholders to coordinate implementation, resolve cross-functional issues, and sustain new capabilities.
Ensure plans, processes, controls, and outcomes align with applicable global, functional, and local regulations, government expectations, and established governance processes.
Qualifications
Bachelor level degree is required, in preferred fields such as Operations, Supply Chain, Business Management, or another related field.
A minimum of 8 years of relevant experience, preferably in program management, with demonstrated ability to prioritize and execute work effectively in a high-pressure environment and a strong focus on process improvement and change management.
Experience in supply chain operations, process excellence, business transformation, or technology-enabled change.
Proven track record of driving global or cross-functional strategic initiatives.
Experience implementing technology solutions in a complex, global environment.
Excellent leadership, collaboration, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to influence at all levels of the organization and lead through ambiguity.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a global mindset and a passion for digital transformation

Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities.

Customer-centered mindset with an interest in simplifying complex processes and improving how people interact with technology.

title: Power & Hydrogen Program Manager, Power & Hydrogen Solutions, GESA
description:
An execution-focused project/program manager responsible for the hands-on coordination and completion of power capacity and hydrogen fuel cell projects across the Amazon fulfillment network. This is a delivery role with a strong bias for action: the PM owns the details, gets into the field, and drives projects from feasibility through commissioning and handover. Oversees multiple concurrent projects spanning temporary and permanent power deployment (utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and air permitting) as well as hydrogen fuel cell execution — including decommissioning of existing assets, launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes, and conversions of existing sites. Sets deadlines, assigns responsibilities, and personally tracks and unblocks progress. Prepares reports for upper management regarding the status of all projects.
Requires a bachelor's degree and at least 4 years of project management experience in power infrastructure, electrical systems, hydrogen/fuel cell systems, or a related area. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, detail-oriented operator who thrives in ambiguity, dives deep into technical and schedule details, and acts with urgency rather than waiting for direction. Must be familiar with a variety of the field's concepts, practices, and procedures across both power and hydrogen domains. Relies on sound judgment to plan and accomplish goals, and is comfortable rolling up sleeves — walking the site, reading the drawings, chasing the long-lead order, and closing out the punch list. Leads and directs the work of contractors, vendors, and cross-functional teams. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected to solve complex energy infrastructure challenges across diverse site conditions and regulatory environments. Typically reports to a manager or head of a unit/department.
Key job responsibilities
Project Management & Bias for Action
- Own delivery end to end and act with urgency — move projects forward every day rather than waiting for direction or escalation
• Get into the details: read the drawings, interrogate the schedule, understand the single-line and the hydrogen P&ID, and verify the numbers personally
• Be hands-on and in the field — walk the site, attend installation and commissioning activities, and verify work directly rather than relying solely on status reports
• Build and maintain the plan of record: detailed schedules, critical-path analysis, dependencies, risks, and clear owners and dates
• Proactively identify blockers and drive them to closure; dive deep on root cause and remove obstacles for contractors and cross-functional teams
• Run a tight operating rhythm — stand-ups, weekly reviews, and crisp written updates that make status and risks unambiguous
• Make decisions with incomplete information, bias toward action, and course-correct quickly as new data emerges
Program Coordination & Oversight
• Responsible for the coordination and completion of multiple simultaneous power and hydrogen execution projects across U.S. sites
• Oversee all aspects of the execution program from feasibility through commissioning and handover
• Set deadlines, assign responsibilities, and monitor and summarize the progress of all projects
• Prepare reports for upper management regarding program status, including monthly flash updates and executive summaries
• Lead and direct the work of contractors, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional teams
• Perform a variety of tasks ranging from technical design review to stakeholder management to regulatory coordination
Amazon Standards, Specifications & Quality Assurance
• Follow and verify that Amazon standards, specifications, and processes are met across all power and hydrogen infrastructure installations
• Ensure electrical equipment, switchgear, generators, fuel cells, hydrogen storage/dispensing systems, and associated systems comply with Amazon technical standards and design requirements
• Conduct quality reviews at each project phase to validate adherence to Amazon specifications before progressing to the next milestone
• Verify vendor deliverables, shop drawings, and equipment submittals meet Amazon engineering standards
• Coordinate with Amazon internal engineering teams to resolve specification questions and obtain approvals
• Document and track any deviations from Amazon specifications, securing proper waivers or corrective actions (e.g., Supplier Corrective Action Reports / SCARs)
Power Capacity Execution
• Drive execution of temporary and permanent power deployment projects — utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and service upgrades
• Oversee deployment of temporary and permanent natural gas and diesel generator systems (1–5MW scale), including rental genset mobilization and conversion to permanent power
• Manage utility coordination including transformer upgrades, switchgear installations, and service upgrades with utility companies
• Own the end-to-end switchgear (SWGR) procurement process: specification development, vendor selection, purchase order issuance, and delivery tracking
• Track SWGR lead times (typically 10–26 weeks) across all sites and ensure orders are placed to meet project timelines; monitor factory acceptance testing (FAT) and coordinate site delivery logistics
• Review and validate electrical designs, single-line diagrams, load calculations, and power distribution configurations
• Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA, and local electrical codes
Hydrogen Fuel Cell Execution
• Decommissioning: Plan and execute safe decommissioning of existing hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cell assets — isolation, purging/inerting, asset removal, site restoration, and disposition in accordance with Amazon standards and applicable safety codes
• Infrastructure & fuel cell launch: Lead the launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes — hydrogen storage and dispensing systems, hydrogen pads, piping, fueling infrastructure, and fuel cell power modules, from design review through installation, commissioning, and startup
• Conversions: Manage conversions of existing sites to hydrogen fuel cell operation (or between configurations), coordinating the transition sequencing, infrastructure modifications, and cutover to minimize operational disruption
• Coordinate with hydrogen fuel cell vendors and OEMs (e.g., Plug Power and equivalents) on equipment specifications, delivery schedules, and field support
• Verify hydrogen systems meet Amazon specifications and applicable hydrogen safety and fire codes (e.g., NFPA 2, NFPA 55) throughout design, installation, and commissioning
• Oversee fuel cell capacity planning, dispenser configuration, and integration with site power and operations
Procurement & Long-Lead Equipment Management
• Own procurement for long-lead equipment across both domains — switchgear, generators, fuel cells, and hydrogen infrastructure components
• Specify, order, track lead times, verify specifications, and coordinate delivery for critical-path equipment
• Coordinate with manufacturers and vendors on custom configurations and delivery schedules
• Escalate equipment delivery risks immediately when lead times threaten project schedules
Permitting & Regulatory
• Own the permitting process for all sites — air permit applications for stationary generator installations and hydrogen-related permits and approvals
• Prepare and submit permit applications across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory environments; track application status, agency review timelines, and approval milestones for each site
• Navigate complex permitting scenarios including CEQA approvals, non-attainment areas, emission offset requirements, and hydrogen/fire code approvals
• Coordinate with environmental and fire/life-safety consultants to develop applications, emission calculations, and hazard analyses
• Maintain a permit tracking log with submission dates, agency contacts, expected approval dates, and required follow-ups
• Proactively identify permitting risks and develop contingency plans to avoid schedule impacts; ensure all required emission and safety data is obtained from generator and fuel cell vendors
Project Execution & Delivery
• Drive the end-to-end project lifecycle: feasibility, design, procurement, permitting, installation, commissioning, and handover
• Develop and maintain detailed project schedules, budgets, risk registers, and status reports
• Coordinate contractor mobilization, equipment procurement, and installation activities
• Identify and resolve critical-path blockers with urgency; escalate issues proactively
• Rely on extensive experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals under compressed timelines
Stakeholder Management
• Serve as the primary point of contact and single-threaded owner across all project stakeholders, aligning internal and external parties and holding each accountable to deliverables and timelines
• Customer — Amazon Operations: partner with Amazon Operations (the internal customer) to understand site requirements, manage expectations, minimize operational disruption, and secure buy-in through launch and handover
• General Contractor (GC): direct and hold the GC accountable for construction scope, schedule, RFIs, submittals, and field execution
• Engineer of Record (EOR) & Architect of Record (AOR): coordinate design intent, drawing reviews, RFIs, and design changes; ensure the installed work conforms to the stamped design
• Electrical Contractor (EC): coordinate electrical installation, terminations, testing, and energization activities and sequencing
• Air permitting agencies & consultants: engage regulatory agencies and environmental consultants (e.g., Trinity) to secure and maintain air permits and keep applications on the critical path
• Utility engagement — gas pipeline: drive utility coordination for natural gas pipeline connections, metering, pressure requirements, service applications, and interconnection timelines
• Equipment vendors & OEMs: manage generator, switchgear, fuel cell, and hydrogen infrastructure vendors on specifications, lead times, and field support
• Coordinate with Property/Construction Managers (PCMs) and Construction Managers at each site
• Provide weekly status updates and monthly program reports to leadership
Site Launches, Commissioning & Energization
• Travel to project sites during critical installation, commissioning, and decommissioning phases
• Oversee equipment startup, testing, and acceptance procedures for both power and hydrogen systems
• Ensure safe energization, hydrogen system startup, and transition to operations

- 4+ years of defining and executing against program timeline & requirements experience
- 4+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams

You'll spend your days partnering with engineering and data science teams to build the agent skills powering our partner sales teams first, then advertising partners directly (automating the workflows our partner and agency development managers run today, laying the foundation for the virtual partner managers partners will use tomorrow). You'll solve delivering expert-level support at scale, composing signals from our partner data layer into agent capabilities that anticipate needs before they ask.

Optics, Touch EE, Display EE, and Mechanical Engineering

Ability to perform computer modeling and simulation with SPICE
Experience in measuring and characterizing IV and CV of TFT devices
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Preferred qualifications: Experience in developing, designing and manufacturing high volume display products

Experience in gate and column driver IC designs

title: Gen AI Portfolio Intake Program Manager
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. We are a diverse collection of thinkers and doers, continually reimagining our products, systems, and practices to help people do what they love in new ways. Everything we build is the result of people in different roles and teams working together to make each other's ideas stronger. That passion for innovation also applies to our internal practices, strengthening our dedication to leave the world better than we found it.
We are seeking a proactive, resourceful, and detail-oriented Gen AI Portfolio Intake Program Manager to join the Project Portfolio Management (PPM) team. You will own the end-to-end intake and refinement of incoming Gen AI project requests, so the highest-value initiatives rise to the top. You will be the single point of contact for requestors. You will apply a consistent scoring framework.
You will also stay abreast of emerging technologies and modern tools. You will look for ways to bring them into daily workflows to improve automation and efficiency for the team and its stakeholders.
In this role, you will bring consistency, accountability, and speed to how Gen AI project requests are evaluated and approved.
Your core focus areas include:
Triage & Prioritization
Request Review: Review new Gen AI project proposals for scope, business impact, data availability, and privacy/compliance considerations.
Scoring & Ranking: Apply a consistent scoring framework (for example, ROI, strategic alignment, risk) to rank and queue requests.
Requirements Gathering & Consolidation
Proactive Engagement: Work with requestors to collect essential details (business goals, ROI estimates, data readiness, privacy constraints) so decisions can be made quickly.
Consolidation: Identify overlapping requests and combine them where it makes sense to streamline intake.
Program Alignment: Align new requests with existing initiatives or programs to avoid duplication.
Stakeholder Management & Communication
Meeting Facilitation: Lead solution review sessions and follow-up meetings to clarify ambiguities, track action items, and resolve blockers.
Single Point of Contact: Give requestors timely status updates and keep the triage process transparent.
Documentation
Centralized Backlog: Maintain a single project backlog that logs request details, decision rationales, and status updates.
Continuous Improvement
Outcome Analysis: Analyze triage outcomes and stakeholder feedback to refine intake forms, scoring models, and meeting cadences.
Standardization: Drive standard templates and processes to speed up future intake and decision-making.
Expectations
Scope: Own the intake lifecycle and scoring model across the full Gen AI request portfolio.
Autonomy: Resolve ambiguity independently.
Process: Design and improve intake forms, scoring models, and governance processes.
Minimum qualifications: BS/BA degree or equivalent practical experience required.
Project & Program Management: 3 - 5+ years of experience in project/program management, PMO operations, or business process improvement. Experience supporting technology, data, or AI/ML teams is preferred.
Intake & Prioritization: Demonstrated ability to triage competing requests and apply a scoring framework (ROI, strategic alignment, risk) to rank and queue work.
Analytical & Business Acumen: Ability to conduct ROI analyses that estimate benefits, costs, and time-to-value for technical initiatives. Ability to translate high-level requirements into actionable compliance checklists.
Governance & Compliance: Hands-on experience with governance processes, data-privacy or risk reviews, or compliance checklists.
Collaboration & Facilitation: Skilled at running efficient stakeholder meetings: setting agendas, capturing action items, and driving decisions. Able to translate technical complexity into clear business terms.
Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication, with the ability to influence cross-functional partners.
Mindset: Self-starter with rigorous follow-up discipline, owning the intake lifecycle from request through handoff. Adaptable, with a continuous-improvement mindset and a passion for optimizing processes.
Attention to Detail: High standard of data integrity and structured organization, and the ability to keep momentum across concurrent work streams in a fast-paced environment.
Preferred qualifications: Experience with AI/ML or Gen AI project delivery.
Experience with capital planning, portfolio prioritization, or resource allocation workflows.
Ability to clearly describe complex processes in written documentation.
Comfort navigating ambiguity while balancing governance with agile execution.
Passion for exploring emerging technologies and productivity tools to automate team workflows.

title: GenAI Research Engineer
description:
Do you believe that generative models can fundamentally change how people interact with devices? Are you excited by the possibility of connecting people to unprecedented levels of creativity? Come join the team that turned cutting edge Generative AI research into compelling user experiences through Apple Intelligence. We are part of the Intelligent System Experiences team at Apple and work on the core modeling technology behind Genmoji, Image Playground and Image Wand. From web-scale datasets to distributed training of foundation models, application specific adapters to on-device optimizations, you will have the unique opportunity to advance and ship state-of-the-art technology that impacts Apple users around the world!
We're looking for a Research Engineer to make these models dramatically faster, smaller and cheaper to run on-device and on server.
You'll work across the whole efficiency stack:
Develop and deploy optimizations algorithms to speed up inference of our production diffusion models (PTQ, QAT, kernel fusion, model distillation).
Design hardware-aware architectures that fit within compute and memory limits with minimal loss of quality.
Own the process end-to-end from prototyping, evaluation to deployment into the Apple ecosystem.
Minimum qualifications: M.S. or PhD in Computer Science or a related field such as Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or equivalent experience.
Deep, demonstrated expertise in at least one of:
Quantization (low-bit and mixed-precision methods, quantization-aware training).
Efficient architecture design, structured pruning or neural architecture search for GenAI or Vision applications.
Strong hands-on experience training and fine-tuning diffusion or other large generative models in PyTorch, JAX, or an equivalent framework.
Comfortable reasoning about efficiency beyond FLOPs, such as memory, latency and numerical precision, and eager to learn hardware-specific constraints.
Excellent cross-functional collaboration skills: You can explain model trade-offs to hardware engineers, hardware constraints to researchers, and integration needs to software teams, in writing and in person.
Preferred qualifications: Publications at CVPR, ICCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR or MLSys on efficient generative models, or significant open-source contributions in this area.

title: Hardware Reliability Engineer - Mac System Reliability
description:
Apple is seeking a Reliability Engineer to join our Mac Hardware Reliability team!
In this role, you’ll collaborate with diverse hardware teams to ensure our products are not only durable and reliable, but also built to exceed expectations. From early concepts to field returns, you’ll lead cross-functional teams, design innovative reliability tests, and drive continuous product improvements.
At Apple, we don’t just follow industry standards—we push beyond them. We value creative problem-solving, dynamic thinking, and the ability to quickly adapt to new technical challenges. If you’re excited about tackling tough problems and shaping the future of amazing products, we’d love to have you on board!
As a System Reliability Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping our products, ensuring longevity by design. You will be responsible for characterizing product usage patterns, translating them into controlled lab tests, and coordinating timely design validation efforts. With these results, you will collaborate through design iterations ensuring our products meet high standards for customer experience.
You bring exceptional problem-solving skills and technical expertise, including:
- A deep understanding of material and device properties (mechanical, electrical, optical, thermal) and the underlying physics
- Proficiency in statistical data analysis and clear reporting, providing design risk assessments and guiding product improvements
- Strong theoretical knowledge in physical failure analysis techniques, such as SEM/EDX/X-Ray and other characterization techniques
- Proven ability to develop new reliability test procedures, create detailed test plans, and analyze results to assess design risks
Additional strengths that will set you apart:
- Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
- Capability to perform tests and troubleshoot issues independently
- Openness to take on new tasks
- A proactive, can-do attitude, with a passion for working alongside an amazing team and innovative products
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in technical field ( mechanical engineering, materials engineering, electrical engineering, physics or related fields) with 2+ years of industry experience
Good written and verbal English communication skills. Ability to effectively communicate through email, WebEx, and phone
Ability to make clear and concise slides and presentations through keynote, excel, etc.
Strong attention to detail and curiosity of how technologies work
Able to use basic productivity apps such as email, web browser, calendar, WebEx/Zoom, spreadsheet, keynote/ppt, etc.
Preferred qualifications: M.S. or PhD in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or an equivalent field
Statistical experience such as Weibull, JMP, or familiarity with accelerated test models
Familiar with Failure Analysis techniques (Optical Microscopy, X-ray/CT, Scanning Electron Microscopy/Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy, etc.), and the ability to use failure analysis methodology to derive a root cause of failure
Collaborative attitude and ability to cross-functionally work effectively
Ability to travel internationally without restriction (up to 10%)

Working knowledge of how large-scale distributed training (JAX/Grain, PyTorch) consumes data across GPU and TPU meshes (global shuffling, sequence packing, deterministic checkpoint and resume, host-to-device memory pipelines).
Track record of setting technical direction across teams, shipping production systems at petabyte scale, and elevating senior engineers.
B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience with formal correctness or high-rigor verification practices (differential parity testing, property-based fuzzing, or state-machine modeling for concurrent commits).

About the Team
The Paid Marketing Analytics team is looking for an experienced Senior Data Scientist to lead brand analytics at DoorDash. This Data Scientist will partner closely with senior Marketing leaders to define our brand measurement approach and guide our brand investment strategy and decision-making. Data Scientists at DoorDash work to uncover insights and turn them into relevant recommendations, driving decisions for the entire organization. Analytics is integral to all operational areas at DoorDash.
About the Role
As a Senior Data Scientist leading brand analytics, you’ll use your quantitative background in brand analytics to define how we measure the impact of brand investment and how brand health affects our business. You’ll report to the leader of Marketing Analytics, and partner closely with our Brand Marketing team. If you enjoy finding patterns amidst chaos, and have experience using brand analytics to affect revenue, growth, and investment, we're looking for someone like you!
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Influence brand strategy, define brand measurement for DoorDash, and play a crucial role in sharing the DoorDash brand externally with our customers.
Partner closely with Marketing leadership to define metrics, KPIs, and a measurement strategy for the DoorDash brand
Work at the intersection of modeling, brand strategy, and business decision making
Use quantitative analysis and the presentation of data to see beyond the numbers and understand what drives our business
Use brand lift survey data, internal metrics, and incrementality testing to create a holistic view of brand impact
Build full-cycle analytics experiments, reports, and dashboards using cutting-edge AI tooling, SQL, R, Python, or other scripting and statistical tools
Be a champion of Brand Analytics within the team and advocate and educate on broader incorporation of leading concepts into Marketing and Consumer plans
Produce recommendations and use statistical techniques and hypothesis testing or causal inference to validate your findings
Provide insights to help business and product leaders understand marketplace dynamics, user behaviors, and long-term trends
Identify and measure levers to help move essential metrics and make recommendations
Work backwards from understanding and sizing problems to ideating solutions
We’re excited about you because you have…
A degree in Math, Physics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or a similar domain
5+ years of experience in brand and marketing analytics owning brand measurement at the intersection of modeling, brand strategy, and business decision making
Demonstrated experience leading the design, implementation, and ongoing operation of an end-to-end brand measurement system, including KPI selection and validation, ongoing brand tracking, campaign lift measurement, and integration with MMM and incrementality testing.
Experience leading brand modeling, working directly with clients, and translating the findings into decisions that drive business growth.
Deep understanding of brand marketing and paid media, with a track record of translating measurement findings into decisions about audiences, investment, and channel mix, and evaluating the relationship between brand health and downstream business outcomes.
Understanding of brand health metrics, consumer attitudes, audience strategy, creative effectiveness, and how media channels contribute across the funnel

MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. Collaborate cross-functionally to win complex deals

Minimum of 5 years consistently meeting and exceeding monthly and quarterly targets

Experience driving consultative, solution-based sales and expanding within strategic industry verticals

description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the team:
The Automation Engineering Team is responsible for delivering robotics-driven automation deployments across a wide range of customer applications. The team partners cross-functionally to translate customer requirements into deployed systems, ensuring solutions are integrated, commissioned, and validated to perform reliably in real manufacturing environments. Automation Engineering works closely with customers, internal technical teams, and external integrators to execute deployments on schedule while maintaining high standards for quality, safety, and repeatability.
About the role:
As Product Manager, Machine Tending, you will own the development, commercialization, and growth of Formic's machine tending offering across both tracks. You will decide which applications we pursue, define standard configurations and pricing, and lead the engineering work that makes them repeatable to deploy.
You will need enough engineering depth to make technical decisions and enough business sense to make commercial ones. You will set direction, get hands-on when needed, and serve as Formic's subject matter expert for the vertical. The goal is an offering Sales can confidently sell, Engineering can consistently deliver, and customers can rely on.
In this role you will:
Own the machine tending product:
Own the strategy, roadmap, and portfolio across third-party and internally developed solutions
Prioritize applications across CNC mills, lathes, machining centers, and press equipment, and define standard configurations and application boundaries
Set requirements for robots, CNC interfaces, workholding, EOAT, controls, software, and safety, favoring compact footprints, quick changeovers, and minimal programming

description:
Job Description:
Continuous Improvement (CI) Specialist
Columbus, OH
Multiple Opportunities
Are you ready to champion a zero-loss culture on the manufacturing shop floor? As a Continuous Improvement (CI) Specialist, you will be the driving force behind loss elimination, providing crucial leadership across all MSE pillars—with a dedicated focus on advancing Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Focused Improvement (FI). In this role, you won't just manage processes; you will empower and upskill frontline operating teams, elevating their technical mastery of process control while partnering directly with Daily Management System (DMS) owners to lock in sustainable operational excellence.
The Continuous Improvement (CI) Specialist is responsible for leading loss elimination and is critical to support all MSE pillars, specifically AM and FI. The CI Specialist is expected to develop the operating teams’ technical understanding and mastery of process control, area operation and to support all Daily Management Systems (DMS) owners.
What are we looking for?
Minimum:
Bachelor’s in Engineering, Supply, Business, or technical field of study or 4 years’ experience in manufacturing with TPM (MSE) participation
3+ years of hands-on experience working within a manufacturing environment utilizing Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Focused Improvement (FI) pillars.
Direct experience executing and maintaining daily Autonomous Maintenance Daily Management Systems, specifically Centerline (CL), Clean, Inspect, Lubricate (CIL), and Abnormality Handling (AH).
Proficiency in basic problem-solving tools (such as the 5 Whys, Fishbone diagrams, and basic Root Cause Analysis) with a track record of applying them to eliminate line losses.
Demonstrated ability to collect, interpret, and report operational and machine performance data.
Experience actively participating in daily operational tier meetings (such as FMOS tier meetings) and communicating technical action plans clearly to a diverse team.
Highly proficient in SAP and the Microsoft Office Suite (specifically Excel, PowerPoint, and Word) to support administrative, operational, and presentation workflows.
Preferred:
Extensive experience and deep subject matter expertise in Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Focused Improvement (FI) pillars.
Proven success in AM and FI pillars, with a documented history of designing and executing line-level training and coaching programs for operators and technical teams.
Experience facilitating Area Loss Analysis and successfully creating and driving 90-day to 1-year area improvement roadmaps that deliver measurable reduction in losses.
Mastery of advanced problem-solving tools (such as Six Sigma Green/Black Belt methodologies, FMEA, or advanced RCPS) to solve complex, chronic chronic losses.
Proven capability to operate effectively within an operational "triad" (partnering proactively with Shift Managers and Technical Owners) to drive a zero-loss culture on the shop floor.
Expert-level understanding of both PDCA and SDCA cycles to systematically transition from standardizing baseline performance to driving continuous improvement.
What are the job responsibilities?
Serve as the on-site Subject Matter Expert (SME) for continuous improvement methodologies, with a dedicated focus on driving the Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Focused Improvement (FI) pillars, while proactively training and upskilling frontline team members.

You will set the standards for how the platform is designed, operated, and supported, and you will deliver dependable, secure, and cost-effective solutions. You’ll gather requirements for new capabilities, stay aware of industry and vendor offerings, and anticipate and mitigate risks with roadmaps and plans.

Behind each of those experiences are the platforms, systems, and operations that help Microsoft bring ideas to market, serve customers, and run at global scale. That's where Microsoft Business Operations (MBO) comes in.
As a Software Engineer in MBO, you'll build the technology that powers Microsoft's business. From the creation of new commercial offers and consumption meters to the systems that track usage, generate insights, enable billing, and measure business outcomes, you'll help shape the end-to-end lifecycle that connects innovation to customer value.
Our engineers operate at the intersection of software, data, AI, and commerce, building intelligent platforms that power some of Microsoft's most critical business processes. You'll work across disciplines to create trusted, scalable systems that provide governance, visibility, and automation from product launch through customer adoption and consumption. The services you build won't just support the business, they'll help define how Microsoft launches, sells, measures, and grows its products around the world.
This is an opportunity to solve complex engineering challenges, influence company-wide platforms, and see your work create impact at a scale few organizations can match.
As a Software Engineer, you will apply computer science principles to design, develop, and optimize software solutions for a set of product features and services. Working with minimal supervision, you will partner with product managers, technical leads, and fellow engineers to understand customer and business requirements and translate them into secure, reliable, scalable, and maintainable solutions.
You will use artificial intelligence (AI) tools and practices across the software development lifecycle in a disciplined manner, taking responsibility for the content of your AI-generated changes to artifacts and applying appropriate tooling and processes. You will apply coding patterns and best practices to build extensible, maintainable code; use logging and telemetry to investigate issues and improve reliability, availability, and performance; and uphold Microsoft standards of security, privacy, safety, and accessibility while collaborating with and learning from more experienced engineers.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
As a Software Engineer, you will contribute across the engineering lifecycle for a set of product features and services - designing, coding, testing, deploying, and operating solutions that are secure, reliable, accessible, and maintainable. You will work with minimal supervision within your feature area, begin to own design decisions under technical leadership, and use AI tools across the development lifecycle in a disciplined manner.
AI-native development. Use AI tools across the full software development lifecycle in a disciplined manner. Take responsibility for the content of your AI-generated changes to artifacts, reviewing all changes and applying appropriate tooling and processes with minimal guidance, and apply Responsible AI practices.
Coding. Create and implement extensible, maintainable code for a product, service, or feature with minimal supervision, reusing code where applicable. Apply coding patterns and best practices, including GenAI-assisted development. Escalate blockers and unknowns and communicate how they impact timelines.
Code reviews. Review product features and test code to ensure it meets team standards, has correct test coverage, and is appropriate for the feature. Bring insight to code reviews to improve code quality and help develop other engineers’ skills, reviewing for coding patterns, security risks, compliance issues, and best practices.
Design and architecture. Provide feedback on architecture proposals under technical leadership, test and explore design options while outlining strengths and weaknesses and begin to own or collaborate on the architecture of solutions. Help ensure designs meet performance, scalability, resiliency, cost (COGS), security, and privacy requirements, and contribute to design documents that support user stories.
Testing and quality. Create a clear test strategy that ensures solution quality and prevents regression with minimal supervision. Add tests to cover gaps, fix or remove broken tests, build testable code, and leverage AI tools for test automation, including security testing to validate security invariants.
Customer requirements. Work with internal stakeholders (e.g., product managers, security/privacy subject matter experts, technical leads) to understand customer and user requirements for a set of features. Incorporate customer insights and continuous feedback loops and advocate for the security and privacy needs of customers.
Dependencies and coordination. Identify dependencies and incorporate them into design documents, understand downstream interactions between systems, and collaborate with other teams to reach common goals where dependencies and validation concerns overlap.
Planning and implementation. Execute project plans, release plans, and work items; contribute to breaking larger work items into smaller ones with estimation; escalate issues that might cause delays; and ensure security, privacy, and compliance requirements are accounted for in planning with minimal guidance.
Deployment and velocity. Support safe deployment to customers by following safe-change practices, contribute to deployment automation targeting zero-touch deployment, monitor dependency status to ensure only the latest secure versions ship, and help identify when rollback plans should be enacted.
Experimentation. Conduct experiments using feature flags and flighting to determine the impact of changes, collaborating with internal partners (e.g., Data Science, product managers) to incorporate success and guard rail metrics.
Engineering excellence. Apply secure design principles and “security as code,” build and share tools that improve engineering efficiency, reuse open-source or internal code responsibly, and stay current with developments that improve availability, reliability, efficiency, observability, and performance.
Live site and reliability. Participate in an on-call rotation as a designated responsible individual (DRI), mitigating live-site issues using least-privilege access and escalating appropriately. Improve troubleshooting guides, telemetry, and tests to make on-call better, respond within SLA, and contribute to logging and instrumentation for monitoring system health, performance, and security.
Security, privacy, and compliance. Apply security best practices, contribute to deployment gates, scanners, and security monitoring, and follow the correct processes for privacy, safety, and accessibility. Maintain an up-to-date understanding of global and local regulations for the technologies you work on.
Collaboration and communication. Communicate clearly and respectfully - verbally and in writing - to drive collaborative, mutually beneficial outcomes; work effectively across teams; and contribute to an inclusive culture and a growth mindset.

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, or related technical discipline with proven experience coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python OR equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Master's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field with proven experience coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 2+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python
OR equivalent experience.
Hands-on experience using artificial intelligence (AI) tools and practices across the software development lifecycle in a disciplined manner, taking responsibility for the content of AI-generated changes to artifacts and reviewing all changes.
Experience applying computer science principles to design, develop, and optimize scalable algorithms, distributed systems, and business applications, including reference architecture and patterns for resilient system design.
Experience in one or more technology domains (e.g., analytics, applications, web, mobile, big data, compute, containers, databases, developer tools, Internet of Things, microservices, or storage).
Experience across the engineering and product lifecycle, including task estimation, design and code review, specification review, bug triage, code check-in, sign-off, test targeting, and performance standards.
Experience with quality assurance processes, measurements, and standards, including test automation and security testing to validate security invariants.
Experience validating solutions and driving improvement by identifying opportunities, and delivering informed, ready designs ahead of production with time for feedback and iteration.
Experience building secure software and meeting regulatory and compliance requirements, including secure coding practices, threat modeling, and privacy considerations.
Experience with logging, telemetry, monitoring, and live-site operations, including on-call/DRI rotations to maintain reliability and availability.
Problem-solving and data analysis skills, applying systems thinking and a data-driven approach to extract actionable insights and make sound decisions in a fast-paced environment.
Experience contributing to code reviews and coaching engineers, reviewing for coding patterns, security risks, and best practices to improve code quality and help develop others’ skills.

OpenAI’s Enterprise Go-To-Market organization helps the world’s largest companies adopt and scale our AI platform across their business from ChatGPT Enterprise to our developer platform and APIs.

Account Associates sit at the front of this motion where technical curiosity turns into executive engagement, and early product signals become enterprise-wide deployments.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Account Associate, you’ll help our Enterprise teams turn product usage, pilots, inbound interest, and targeted outreach into qualified enterprise opportunities. Working alongside Account Directors, you’ll apply your sales experience to discovery, stakeholder mapping, and account strategy while deepening your ability to navigate complex enterprise opportunities.  You’ll exercise judgment in handling discovery and qualification assignments, evaluating differing stakeholder needs and recommending next steps while drawing on Account Directors for guidance on more complex issues.

We are looking for individuals with 2–4 years of professional sales experience in SDR/BDR roles, full-cycle Account Executive roles, or a combination of both. Candidates should be motivated to build on that experience and grow into world-class enterprise sellers. This role can lead to opportunities as an Account Director or in other GTM roles, with progression based on performance and business needs rather than a fixed timeline.

For the right person, this is an opportunity to build on an established sales foundation and develop a long-term career in AI go-to-market.

This role is based in Austin, TX. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week (Monday through Wednesday) and offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Partner with Account Directors on account strategy, multi-threading, and deal progression.  Assess account developments and recommend adjustments to engagement approaches within agreed priorities.

 - Lead high-quality discovery to uncover business priorities, map stakeholders, and assess enterprise readiness.  Evaluate differing stakeholder needs and incomplete information to recommend qualification decisions and next steps.

 - Contribute to pipeline reviews by sharing outbound activity, account insights, and early competitive signals.

 - Build and iterate on AI-enabled GTM workflows (GPTs/agents) to scale prospecting and qualification.

 - Have 2–4 years of professional sales experience in SDR/BDR roles, full-cycle Account Executive roles, or a combination of both, with demonstrated success in your assigned responsibilities. Experience working at a startup or selling enterprise SaaS is strongly preferred.

 - Have a track record of meeting or exceeding quota or measurable sales targets, such as qualified pipeline, sales opportunities, or revenue, with clear examples of your individual contribution.

 - Demonstrate strong business acumen and can lead discovery conversations that uncover customer priorities, connect potential solutions to measurable outcomes, and establish clear next steps.

 - Have experience researching accounts, developing targeted outreach, and engaging business and technical stakeholders to generate qualified opportunities. Experience prospecting into enterprise or strategic accounts is a plus.

 - Have a strong interest in AI, regularly experiment with AI tools, and can connect their capabilities to practical business needs.

 - Use performance data and feedback to refine your approach, and show persistence when outreach or opportunities do not progress as expected.

 - Are comfortable with ambiguity, moving quickly, and taking ownership of your work while collaborating closely with Account Directors.

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

title: Manager, Sourcing - MTO (Jewelry)
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Sourcing Manager, MTO (Jewelry)
We are seeking a  Sourcing Manager, MTO to own and drive the complete made-to-order workflow for jewelry—from order placement through final customer delivery—ensuring our 3-week fulfillment promise is met reliably, with zero defects and exceptional customer experiences. Reporting to the VP of Sourcing, the ideal candidate will leverage jewelry manufacturing expertise, meticulous operational discipline, real-time visibility into production workflows, and an obsessive commitment to quality and delivery to scale our partnership model and prove that speed, quality, and affordability can coexist.
Success in this role means consistently delivering 98%+ on-time delivery, maintaining first-pass yield of ≥98%, achieving zero customer returns attributable to manufacturing defects, building a real-time order tracking system that provides complete visibility from factory to end customer, and enabling Quince to scale jewelry MTO volume while maintaining the highest quality standards. This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our business, build a world-class supply chain partnership, and shape the future of how premium jewelry is made and delivered.
Responsibilities
Own end-to-end production planning and scheduling across manufacturing partners; translate demand forecasts into detailed daily/weekly production workflows that meet the 3-week delivery window.
Build and operate a real-time order tracking system with complete visibility from order intake through factory production, QC, packing, shipment, and final customer delivery; ensure ≥98% data accuracy and daily updates.
Establish and maintain quality control standards across manufacturing partners; monitor defect rates, first-pass yield, escalate quality misses immediately.
Serve as primary operational liaison with manufacturing partners and conduct weekly operational reviews covering schedule adherence, quality, delivery performance, capacity, and risk mitigation with domestic and international suppliers.
Coordinate logistics and fulfillment; ensure correct packaging, labeling, and shipment to freight forwarders; track deliveries through final customer receipt and manage any post-delivery issues.
Create daily MTO standup and weekly operational dashboard tracking on-time delivery, defect rates, lead times, inventory levels, and production bottlenecks; provide monthly reporting to leadership.
Monitor and respond to production risks in real-time; flag orders at risk of missing the 3-week window within 24 hours; drive rapid problem-solving across manufacturing, quality, and logistics.
Qualifications
Required:
Minimum 5 years of jewelry manufacturing experience, including direct exposure to Jewelry manufacturing, quality control, and production management processes.
Proven track record of managing production workflows, schedules, and timelines in jewelry or related manufacturing environments, with experience delivering on accelerated timelines.
Direct experience tracking orders and managing fulfillment from factory through shipping and customer delivery (end-to-end visibility and accountability).
Demonstrated ability to manage quality control, defect tracking, root-cause analysis, and corrective action closure in a production environment.
Strong experience coordinating with manufacturing partners or managing supplier relationships in production-critical roles; comfort with cross-partner communication and escalation.
Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills and experience building or managing production tracking systems (ERP, MES, custom dashboards); ability to learn new software tools quickly.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfort with data-driven decisions and identifying process improvements from operational metrics.
Exceptional written and verbal communication; ability to create clear, actionable reports and escalation summaries for multiple stakeholders.
Obsessive attention to detail; defects and missed deadlines are intolerable to you; you catch problems before they reach customers.
Calm under pressure; ability to manage competing priorities and operational escalations with composure and rapid decision-making.
Collaborative and relationship-oriented; you build strong partnerships with manufacturing teams, quality leads, logistics partners, and cross-functional stakeholders.
Experience working cross-functionally with merchandising, sourcing, and production teams

title: AVP, Federal Sales
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role
Samsara is building its Federal business, and we're looking for the Sales leader who will build out the team and strategy. As the AVP of Federal Sales, you will be the first and most senior specialized Federal hire, accountable for taking the Samsara Connected Operations Cloud into U.S. federal civilian agencies as part of Phase 1 and defense agencies as part of Phase 2 on a dedicated, FedRAMP-authorized government cloud environment.
Federal agencies run some of the largest vehicle and asset fleets in the world, and they are modernizing how they manage safety, maintenance, sustainability, and mission readiness. Samsara already partners with state and local government agencies across the country, including statewide programs. This role turns that foundation into a durable federal practice.
You will operate as the leader of a dedicated federal practice: you'll design the team, hire it, set the go-to-market strategy, shape our partner and contract-vehicle approach, and own federal bookings. You'll work hand in hand with Product, Security and Compliance, Legal, Marketing, Partnerships, and Revenue Operations to make Samsara easy for federal agencies to buy and trust. This role reports to the Vice President of Public Sector Sales.
This is a remote position open to candidates based on the East Coast (Maine, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, and Florida), with a preference for candidates based in the Washington D.C. metropolitan area. This position requires travel up to 40% of the time.
In this role, you will:
Build and own Samsara's federal go-to-market strategy for civilian agencies, including agency prioritization, territory design, and a multi-year plan that sequences investment against certification milestones and the federal budget cycle - with a plan to expand to defense agencies in the future
Build Samsara's federal route-to-market with Partnerships: distributors and resellers, contract vehicles such as GSA MAS and GWACs, and co-sell relationships with federal systems integrators
Hire, develop, and lead a dedicated federal team of account executives, future business development and capture managers, and solutions engineers, starting with a focused pod and scaling headcount as pipeline and bookings prove out
Own federal pipeline and bookings, with clear leading indicators (agency relationships, qualified opportunities, RFI and proposal activity) in the early stage and full bookings accountability once the authorized product is available to transact
Develop senior relationships with agency fleet, logistics, operations, and CIO/CISO leaders, and represent Samsara at industry days, federal events, and with government affairs partners
Partner with Security and Compliance and Product to translate FedRAMP authorization progress into a clear, accurate customer narrative and to bring agency requirements back into the GovCloud roadmap
Work with Revenue Operations, Finance, and Sales Compensation to design federal-specific pipeline stages, forecasting, quotas, and compensation plans for long-cycle selling
Partner with Legal, Deal Desk, and Contracts on FAR-compliant terms, teaming agreements, and federal ethics requirements, setting a high bar for compliance across the team
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
Minimum requirements for the role:
12+ years of enterprise technology sales experience, with 8+ years selling to U.S. federal government agencies
5+ years leading federal sales teams, including leaders of account executives, as a second-line manager or above
Track record of building or scaling a federal sales practice at a commercial-first SaaS, cloud, or IoT company, including selling through and after FedRAMP authorization
Consistent over-achievement of federal bookings targets, with closed multi-year, seven-figure agency contracts
Hands-on experience with federal acquisition: GSA Schedule and other contract vehicles, distributor and reseller models, and teaming with federal systems integrators
Established relationships with federal civilian agency stakeholders, systems integrators, and the federal partner ecosystem
Experience leading business development and capture for competitive federal procurements, from pre-RFP shaping through proposal and award
Eligibility to obtain a Public Trust position
An ideal candidate also has:
A network that includes experienced federal sellers, capture managers, and solutions engineers who would follow them to a new practice
Experience co-selling with federal systems integrators inside a direct sales organization, including clear account ownership and compensation rules
Familiarity with Shipley or a comparable capture and proposal methodology
Experience designing activity-based or MBO compensation for federal teams before authorized product is available
Working knowledge of FedRAMP, FAR/DFARS, Section 508 accessibility, and Buy American and Trade Agreements Act requirements, and how they show up in deals
Experience with Department of Defense or National Guard fleet programs, as a foundation for future expansion

Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role
AI is changing how our R&D organization builds and runs software. This is a new role: one leader for Samsara's AI bets across the software development lifecycle. You'll own two efforts that started and whatever comes next.
Dev Agents builds in-house and integrates vendors such as Claude and Codex. That includes an Agent Gateway that serves internal MCPs, managed access to skills, and cloud runners that fan work out to cloud agents.
SRE AI is an agent that does the first-line work of an on-call engineer. It already runs on real incidents in production: it writes a root cause analysis, escalates severity when it has proof, and can roll back the deployment it identified as the cause.
This is a new role. You'll lead a team of five to 10 senior engineers, from Senior to Staff. You'll work directly with every R&D leader and with the developers who use what you build.
This is a remote position open to candidates based in North America.
What makes this unique
One leader across the lifecycle. You own AI for the whole software development lifecycle, for our R&D organization.
Room to try things. Try, fail, learn. One bet in five landing is a good outcome.
Already in production. SRE AI runs on live incidents today, and two teams use it as first responder.
A senior team. Principal, senior staff, staff and senior engineers who work without a roadmap.
Build, don't hand off. This is hands-on leadership. You'll work from the details, not from a PRD.
Why this role matters
Real-world impact at scale
Engineers on every team take turns on-call, which costs roughly 10 to 15 percent of headcount. The goal is an agent that is first responder to every page, so people are only woken up when a human is needed, and arrive with the root cause in hand.
Make SRE AI first responder for five teams, and the default for every team by the end of 2027.
Within 12 months, the median developer ships as fast as today's 90th percentile.
Unique technical challenges
Choose which experiments to run for a root cause analysis agent when no playbook exists.
Decide when to build, integrate or buy as model prices and capabilities shift roughly every quarter.
Earn trust for automated actions, such as severity escalation and rollbacks.
Raise output without raising load on engineers, with cost per pull request (token spend plus infrastructure) as the measure.
Be on the founding team of AI agent factories: Within three months, stand up an end-to-end system for campaign-style work: backfilling tests, fixing recurring logging problems, and drive changes, etc.
You should apply if:
You want to own an AI bet at scale. You'd like one leader's view across how an entire R&D organization builds, ships and runs software.
You build to learn. You'd rather try the latest technology than read about it, and you can say what failed.
You like working without a roadmap. You set direction yourself, and you move when nobody has told you to.
You lead senior engineers by earning their trust. Principal and staff engineers follow you because you're in the details with them.
You care what things cost. Tokens and infrastructure are part of the design, not an afterthought.
